absent: Numeric values of frequency QoS defaults, PM QoS sentinels, request types and action semantics.
Implementation, locking and notification ordering of pm_qos helpers, plist handling and blocking notifier delivery.
Full layout of frequency constraints and request objects and definition of the active-request predicate.
Memory bitmap operations, radix traversal, cursor movement, iteration order and concurrency rules.
Saveable page criteria, free page marking, zone accounting and high memory buffer management.
Direct map manipulation, TLB flush scope, debug pagealloc behavior and address mapping guarantees.
Platform suspend and idle operation structures, state validity rules, system sleep guard semantics and waiter mechanics.

findings.text: Frequency constraints initializer prepares minimum and maximum constraint objects with their respective defaults and readies associated notification chains for later registration.
Frequency QoS value reader returns the effective minimum or maximum, substituting built-in defaults when the container is missing and reporting misuse for unknown request kinds.
Frequency QoS add operation validates container, request storage and value, rejects already active requests, then binds the request to its container and type with cleanup on failure.
Frequency QoS update operation validates request and value, requires an active binding, treats unchanged values as success without further work, otherwise forwards the new value.
Frequency QoS remove operation validates and requires an active binding, forwards removal with the default sentinel, then detaches the request from its container.
Frequency QoS notifier add registers a blocking observer on the minimum or maximum chain after validating container and observer, rejecting unknown kinds.
Frequency QoS notifier remove unregisters a blocking observer from the minimum or maximum chain after validating container and observer, rejecting unknown kinds.
Frequency QoS apply dispatcher routes add, update and remove actions to the minimum or maximum constraint according to request type, failing for unknown types.
Safe page allocator provides an address-sized integer result for a single securely obtained page using the supplied allocation mask.

Nosave region registration records a page frame interval excluded from hibernation images, ignoring empty intervals and coalescing contiguous intervals with the prior entry while logging the covered range.

Hibernation image creation interface counts saveable and high memory pages, verifies sufficient free memory including input-output reserve, allocates image storage, copies contents, and reports copy, zero and metadata counts with out-of-memory failure.

Platform sleep operation installers publish suspend and idle operation tables under system sleep protection and refresh visible sleep state names and current selection according to platform validity and configured default.
Idle wake request moves an active suspend-to-idle session toward wake and signals one waiter, leaving idle state untouched when no session is active.
Suspend predicates expose whether the current sleep selection is the idle default and whether only the deepest state is accepted on this platform.
A frequency QoS value is invalid only when negative and different from the default sentinel, so all non-negative values and the sentinel itself are accepted.
Minimum frequency constraints use maximum aggregation semantics while maximum constraints use minimum aggregation, each starting with target, default and unconstrained values set to its own default.
An inactive frequency request has no container binding while an active one is bound, with binding cleared after failed addition and after removal.
Each frequency constraint kind owns a dedicated notification chain, and registration always selects the chain matching the requested minimum or maximum kind.
Reading a missing or erroneous frequency container never dereferences it and instead yields the built-in minimum or maximum default for that kind.
Nosave intervals are accumulated in sorted order so that only the tail needs checking for contiguity, and inverted or empty intervals leave state unchanged.
Total saveable image pages equal copied pages plus all-zero pages, with metadata size proportional to total entries packed per page.
Hibernation copying uses direct access when the source page is already present and otherwise brackets the copy with temporary mapping and unmapping.
Copies involving high memory use local mappings, employing an intermediate buffer when only the destination is high to avoid disturbing source contents through mapping side effects.
Image admission requires free low memory beyond requested pages plus a fixed input-output reserve, after accounting for already allocated image pages and outstanding high memory needs.

Suspend name tables provide fixed labels for the three suspend states alongside sleep names, with current and default selections evolving only through boot option parsing and platform operation installation.
Hibernation and general suspend logging each use a distinct constant message prefix identifying the subsystem for all messages from those files.
Installation of suspend and idle operation tables holds the system sleep guard across the update and associated state table refresh.
Idle wake checks and updates the idle state under a raw spinlock with interrupts saved, signalling a waiter only when transitioning out of an active suspend.
Frequency QoS notification chains are blocking, so registration, unregistration and delivery occur in sleepable context and must not be invoked from atomic sections.
Linked page fragment holds a next link plus a data area filling the remainder of one page, stored packed without padding.
Chain allocator tracks a chain head, bytes used in the current page, an allocation mask, and a flag requiring only safe pages.
Radix node pairs list linkage with a pointer to a page-sized array of bitmap words used for zone tracking.
Per-zone bitmap radix header links zones together, maintains separate node and leaf lists, records start and end frame numbers, points at the root, and stores level and block counts.
Memory bitmap aggregates zone headers, backing pages for bitmap storage, and a cursor recording current zone, node, node and current frame numbers, and bit position.
Memory extent entry holds list linkage with start and end addresses delimiting a contiguous interval.
Nosave region entry holds list linkage with start and end frame numbers delimiting excluded memory.
High memory restore entry pairs copy and original page pointers with a next link forming a singly linked list.
Frequency request moves from detached to attached on successful add, remains attached across updates, and returns to detached on remove, with misuse of the current state warned and rejected.
Idle suspend state remains unchanged when idle or already waking, and otherwise advances from any active suspend substate to wake exactly once per wake request.
Sleep selection starts from boot option values then is refined when platform operations appear, promoting standby or deep states to current only when valid and preferred by the configured default.
Image creation progresses through sizing, admission, allocation, copying and accounting, with early exit on insufficient memory or allocation failure and zero pages excluded from copied counts.
Suspend alarm test prefers deep, then shallow, then idle states on successive failures, repeating the whole attempt up to a configured count before disabling the alarm.
Low-level visible image creation entry callable from outside C, reporting success or out-of-memory without exposing internal bitmap handling.
Early boot option parser maps textual sleep names to internal states and seeds both current and default selections.
Early suspend test drives real suspend attempts using a real-time clock alarm, selecting fallback states and handling repeat counts.
Device matcher identifies real-time clock candidates that support alarms and whose parent may wake the system.
Misuse such as adding an active request, updating or removing an inactive one, or supplying an unknown constraint kind triggers a warning and an invalid argument failure.
Failures to change direct mapping protections during hibernation mapping produce a one-time warning while allowing the copy to proceed.
Partial image allocation on failure is released before reporting out-of-memory, preventing leaked image pages from skewing later admission checks.
Nosave region bookkeeping assumes allocation never fails and aborts on failure, so callers must only invoke it where such termination is acceptable.
Page copying simultaneously detects all-zero contents by accumulating word values, allowing zero pages to be recorded in a separate bitmap and their storage slot reused.
Linked page payload capacity equals one page minus the size of a single pointer.
Bitmap end marker is all bits set, with block capacity measured in bits per page and shift plus mask values derived from page geometry.
Radix level shift has two build-dependent forms differing by one bit, with the level mask covering exactly the bits selected by the active shift.
Encoded frame numbers reserve the most significant bit as a zero-page flag, leaving remaining bits for the actual frame number.
Image page allocation combines normal kernel reclaimable semantics with suppression of allocation failure warnings.
Fixed operational counts include a watchdog batch of one hundred twenty eight times one thousand twenty four pages, a ten second suspend test interval, and a five unit suspend test delay.
Page safety selectors use zero for any and for keep-unsafe, and one for safe and for clear-unsafe.
Restore entries per linked page equals the linked payload capacity divided by the size of one restore entry.
User-visible suspend names map the three suspend states to short labels and separately to sleep names.
